programmes.d: Prompted by news of a flight attendant's brutal murder, the son of a previous victim contacts police. Both murders have similar MOs, and biological evidence proves that these were serial killings.
The woman had been sexually assaulted, stabbed repeatedly, and left for dead.
When a college student vanished without a trace, her fellow students were concerned about her safety and their own.
Tracey Frame, 35, was convicted of killing David Nixon after he planned to end their relationship.

In the early hours of a morning just before Christmas, a college student was abducted from the parking lot of her apartment. Her body was found later that day; she had been sexually assaulted and shot at point-blank range.
When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action.

In 2002, funeral director Lonnie Turner, Sr. was found shot to death. His son Lonnie Jr. became the prime suspect, particularly after it was discovered that the murder was committed with his gun. However, he had an alibi for the time of the murder.
A man becomes the prime suspect in the deaths of his parents as police examine mud and blood traces.
Almost 50 years later, advances in technology identified a murderer who had been free.
A man dies in his home after a long history of heart disease. A few weeks after the funeral, rumors surface that the death was no accident.
A lifelong resident in a Tasmania town was murdered. Robbery appeared to be the motive.

A fifteen-year-old boy dies from a mysterious gunshot wound to the head while sitting in the lobby of his father's gun club. Ballistics, laser technology, made-to-scale models and the latest in forensic animation are used to find the cause.
In 2000, Judy Southern arrived home from work and was shot by a gunman waiting within.

A man riding a bicycle was fatally injured in what police believed to be a hit-and-run accident. Tiny clues found at the scene created a picture of the vehicle which struck him and led police to its driver.
A mother's suicide is not convincing when an attempt on her life three years prior is discovered.

Fire engulfs the home where Lori Keidel and her siblings were left alone while their father went to the laundromat. Years after her mother's disappearance, Lori tells police she witnessed her mother's death.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.
In 1962, the small town residents of Hanford, California lost their sense of peace when one of their own, 15-year-old Marlene Miller, was murdered.
Forensic psychiatry helps a wife to remember the details of how her husband was shot.

A man is found dead in his home and his ex-wife has a perfect alibi. To determine time of death, investigators need to know when the victim ate his last meal. An endocrinologist, a forensic botanist and a short-order cook answer their question.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on robberies which targeted tourists in Florida.

A fire erupts in Kings Cross Station in London, killing 31 people and injuring dozens more. Investigators pinpoint the cause of the fire, but it takes state-of-the-art technology and fluid dynamics experts to explain why it became a deadly inferno.
A brilliant architect became ill and died just before she was to testify in a criminal trial.

Doctors are puzzled when a two-year-old boy is rushed to the hospital with brain seizures and breathing difficulties. Finally, the boy's sister provides an important clue, raising the possibility of a rare syndrome.
When two boys are brutally attacked, investigators rely on evidence fished out of a nearby pond.

A woman's death in Pennsylvania triggers a homicide investigation into another woman's death in North Carolina. Faced with striking similarities, examiners must determine if their suspect's story about accidental drowning is all wet.
A serial bomber was waging a vendetta against the legal profession.
In 1987, the death of Crystal Purcell was considered an accident. Then in 2001, Barbara Purcell called police to suggest that her estranged husband had killed Crystal.
In 1991, San Francisco pornographer Artie Mitchell was murdered in his home.

A married couple decided to escape the cold of winter with a mini-vacation in Key West. The wife went missing and police searched every square inch of the island; they found nothing but a pair of sandals which might have belonged to her.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe-print, several foreign hairs and unknown fingerprints.
Paul Gruber's daughter suspected something was wrong when she received birthday cards addressed from her father, but written in a stranger's handwriting.
In 1984, California firefighters battled ten arson fires in three weeks.

The 1987 disappearance of Houston resident Tracy Jo Shine is recalled. The investigation went cold until 2000 when a "cold case squad" learned that the woman's ex-boyfriend Michael Neal had bragged about killing her.
A physics professor and NASA technology help to catch a killer.

A healthy young man dies mysteriously in his sleep and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine in his blood. Investigators find a suicide note and presume he killed himself until a forensic linguist examines the note.
In 2006, Texas real estate agent Sarah Anne Walker was found brutally murdered in a model home.

Seattle police had no suspects in the violent murder of grunge singer Mia Zapata. More than a decade passed before evidence collected by a prescient medical examiner could be used by forensic scientists to identify the killer.
Cutting-edge technology proves the police arrested the wrong suspect in a young girl's murder case.
In 1969, 25-year-old phone operator Diane Maxwell was raped and murdered. Her brother promised he'd find out who was responsible and bring the killer to justice.
Woman disappears from grocery store parking lot in Boulder; investigators find extraordinary clues.
The medical examiner ruled the death an accident, but the detectives investigating the case thought the evidence at the scene indicated otherwise.
A woman disappears without a trace, along with two others who vanished under similar circumstances.
Notepad points to kidnapper.
When a victim is brutally murdered in his own bed, investigators find a shoe impression in the mud outside — physical evidence they hope will lead to the killer.
The murder of a couple puzzles investigators until the victims' dog leads police to the killer.

Robert Sims returns home after working the night shift and finds his wife unconscious on the kitchen floor. Their son is fast asleep in an upstairs bedroom, but their six-week-old daughter, Heather, is missing.
Using an anonymous letter and geographical profiling, investigators close in on a serial rapist.

In 2000, construction manager Darrell North was found dead in his work trailer in Ft. Worth, Texas. When investigators arrived, they found that he had been stabbed 46 times, indicating a personal relationship between the victim and the attacker.
In a rich suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to what appeared to be an accidental drowning.

In little more than a month, two women who lived in the same apartment complex were brutally murdered. The similarities of the crime scenes led police to conclude they were dealing with a serial killer who harbored an intense hatred of women.
Security cameras in a casino tracked a woman's movements until right before she disappeared.

A young woman suddenly becomes critically ill, eventually leaving her unable to walk. A bone marrow test reveals the cause: arsenic poisoning. Investigators must determine if the poisoning was caused by groundwater contamination or something sinister.
Lives changed in the 20 years following an unsolved murder, and so did forensic science.
In 1999, Patrick McRae was found dead in his Des Moines home and the crime scene was awash with blood. Analysis showed it had come from two people, one of whom was female.
When a college student is found dead, evidence suggests that he knew his killer. With just three hairs and some microscopic cells, police unravel a web of lies and find the motive for murder.
All evidence leads to the wife when a real estate developer is murdered.
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people.

When police find the body of 11-year-old Krista Harrison, there are few clues to the killer's identity. But authorities are intrigued by unusual orange fibers embedded in clothing found near the victim.
A serial killer was on the loose and police had to find him before he struck again.
In a 1992 murder case, the autopsy of a cremated body turns up telltale clues of foul play.
Foul play is suspected when Fort Worth factory worker Glenda Furch disappears after her shift.
When a young fireman died from what appeared to be serious but undiagnosed heart disease, his family and friends had no proof of foul play.
In 2007, Brian & Beverly Mauck were found dead in their Graham, Washington home.

The investigation into the kidnapping and rape of an 18-year-old Ohio woman is aided when the victim returns hours after the incident occurred. With her help, the police are able to track the assailant to his front door.
The difficulty in solving bombings.
In 1993, 82-year-old Kathryn Bishop was found dead in her Pennsylvania home. Tiny clues on the victim's body would tell police what happened that night.
A painstaking investigation leads police to a lawyer husband with a motive to kill his wife.
A lifelong resident of the tiny town of Lefroy, Tasmania was murdered outside his own home. Robbery appeared to be the motive, but with no suspects, the investigation came to a halt.
A drive-by shooting leaves one man dead and another seriously wounded.

In the summer of 1986, Kathleen Lipscomb's body was found on a deserted road outside of San Antonio. Months and years passed, but the crime was never solved. Finally, a private investigator discovered Kathleen's diary.
In 1989, 4-year-old April Loveless was found dead in the backyard of her Texas home.
A murder investigation in Florida crosses jurisdictions from New York and Jamaica. The police rely on cell phone mapping, wiretapping and a host of forensic evidence to link a suspect to a murder.
While Earl Morris was vacationing in California, he learned his wife had gone missing.
In 1991, Grand Junction, Colorado is on edge after a series of deadly bombings kill two people and injure one more. Police race to find the culprit before he strikes again.
On Christmas eve 2005, the corpse of a black male is found burning near Baltimore.
A Michigan State University grad student disappeared and was presumed dead. With the help of a professor of geological sciences, police hoped to get the "dirt" on her killer.
A grad student disappeared and a professor of geological sciences helped police in the search.

In this classic episode of Forensic Files, the longest-running true crime series in television history, Eileen and Derrick Severs disappear from their home in a small village in Great Britain and police find evidence of foul play.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal.

In 1980, Michigan resident Shannon Mohr died in what her new husband, David Davis, reported to be a horseback riding accident. After her death, Shannon's family reported that Davis seemed far from grief-stricken.
Body found in a salvage shop.

On Christmas Eve 2005, a man's body is found burning near Baltimore. He's eventually identified as 26-year-old Wesley Person. Distinctive building materials from the 1930s play a crucial role in solving this case.
When an off-duty policeman was shot dead, his fellow officers were determined to solve the crime.
In 1996, Virginia Beach police arrive at the Makdessi apartment to find the bloodied bodies of Elise Makdessi and Navy sailor Quincy Brown. But was Brown Elise's lover or her assailant?
Investigating a Colorado hunter shot and killed; police suspect two murder weapons and two killers.

No one in a quiet residential community saw anything unusual the day one of their neighbors was brutally attacked and murdered. Fingerprints found at the crime scene and surveillance video helped investigators to apprehend the presumed killer.
A brilliant architect became ill and died just before she was to testify in a criminal trial.

When hunters reported finding a skull in a Texas canyon, police immediately began an investigation. With a forensic artist's reconstruction, police eventually learned the victim's identity. Now all they had to do was find her killer.
The sudden appearance of thick fog causes a 99-car accident on I-75 in Tennessee, killing 12.
A suspicious fire swept through an apartment killing two young women.

When Kristine Fitzhugh failed to show up for her music class, her husband found her dead at the bottom of the stairs of their Palo Alto home. Further investigation reveals evidence of murder in the kitchen.
New York police hunt the Zodiac killer after a series of deadly attacks.

Police investigate a discarded sleeping bag containing bloody sneakers and a purse, which eventually leads to the body of a young woman. A mark found on the victim's body enables police to track the killer.
When two boys are brutally attacked, investigators rely on evidence fished out of a nearby pond.

A suspicious fire sweeps through an apartment, killing two young women. The cause of the fire and the identity of the victims are unclear, but a closer look at the scene reveals something hidden in the ashes.
An assailant avoids the law for 16 years due to a lack of evidence.
When two boys are brutally attacked, investigators rely on evidence fished out of a nearby pond. It became the first case where diatom analysis was used to place a suspect at the scene of the crime.
An 18-month-old skeleton found on marshland puts forensics to the ultimate test.
